test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A ball of diameter 10 cm is placed at a distance of 40 cm in front of a lens with a power of +5.0 D. The diameter of the image of the ball will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1: 10 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The power of the lens (P) is given as +5.0 D (diopters), which means it is a converging lens.
 
• The focal length (f) of the lens is calculated using the formula f = 1/P. Therefore, f = 1/5 = 0.2 meters (20 cm).
 
• The object distance (u) is given as 40 cm in front of the lens. Since it is in front of the lens, it is taken as negative, hence u = -40 cm.
 
• Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, we can find the image distance (v). Substituting the given values, we get 1/20 = 1/v + 1/40, solving for v gives us v = 40 cm. The magnification (m) is given by m = v/u. Therefore, m = 40/-40 = -1. Hence, the image diameter is the same as the object diameter, which is 10 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lens Power (P)**

 
 
• The power of a lens is a measure of its ability to converge or diverge light.
 
• It is given in diopters (D), where P = 1/f (in meters).
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f)**
 
 
• The focal length of a lens is the distance from the lens at which parallel rays of light converge or appear to diverge after passing through the lens.
 
• It is positive for converging (convex) lenses and negative for diverging (concave) lenses.
 
 
 
• **Object Distance (u)**
 
 
• The distance between the object and the lens.
 
• It is taken as negative if the object is on the same side as the incoming light (real object).
 
 
 
• **Image Distance (v)**
 
 
• The distance between the image and the lens.
 
• It is taken as positive if the image is on the opposite side of the incoming light (real image).
 
 
 
• **Magnification (m)**
 
 
• The ratio of the height (or diameter) of the image to the height (or diameter) of the object.
 
• It is given by m = v/u.
